CBMADT: Ngwelezana Hospital Paediatric Burns Unit

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We showcase the new pediatric burns unit at Ngwelenzana Hospital built by the Carte Blanche Making A Difference Trust

Unique Selling Point:
The latest project of the Carte Blanche Make A Difference Trust looks set to make a profound impact for the people of Umhlathuze municipality. The Ngwelezana Hospital is the recipient of a new paediatric burns unit thanks to the trust. This new facility will be able to cater for 22 children providing a range of care options ranging for general patients, High Care and isolated ICU Rooms. It will provide essential clinical wet & dry treatment areas and unique custom-designed air treatment facilities.

Carte Blanche investigates just how this new state of the art facility will change lives through an intimate look at the experience of a patient and that of a doctor in the new burns unit

Summary:
We celebrate the opening of the new paediatric burns unit at the Ngwelezana Hospital. This is the culmination of a 2-year project spearheaded by the Carte Blanche Making A Difference Trust.

In this story we will look at how this burns unit will change the lives of children who experienced horrific burn injuries. We will see the facilities in operation and paint a very human portrait of the benefits of this new unit, as seen though the eyes of doctor & patient

Press Release:


From paraffin stoves, open flames and candles falling over – the chances of a child suffering severe burns increases in poorly developed areas - is a common reality in South Africa. Now the Carte Blanche Making a Difference Trust together with its valued partners and donors, have stepped in to create a custom designed Paediatric Burns Unit at Ngwelezana Hospital, which is a key referral centre for many children in Kwazulu Natal. This facility aims to provide the highest level of care for children suffering from severe burn injuries.

Script:


OPENING V/O: Burns are one of the 5 leading causes of child injury mortality in South Africa. For most parents, our children are our reason for living. So when they are injured in such a tragic way, our worlds fall apart. Who do we turn to? Where do we go?

MACFARLANE: It’s a mother’s worst nightmare: a normal day that begins an ordinary bath drawn for a child. A back turned for a split second and all of a sudden a child’s cry and then you realise something has gone horribly wrong.

Nokthula tells the story of how baby Nonthubheko was injured

V/O: Not only was her baby, Nonthubheko badly injured, but Nokthula is without medical aid.

MACFARLANE ( EXTERIOR, TOWNSHIP IN BACKGROUND): That’s the dilemma facing millions of South Africans who don’t have access to private hospitals. There only option is to turn to public healthcare. In a rural area like this one in the heart of Kwa Zulu Natal, that takes them to Ngwelezana Hospital.

V/O: Ngwelezana Tertiary Hospital is located close to Empangeni and services around 2.4 million people of the Umhlathuze Municipality. It is the only hospital to offer specialist treatment in the area.

They receive many burn victims (especially now that it’s winter in South Africa), as hospital CEO Dr Bright Madlala explains

Dr Bright Madlala on burn patients

This is where baby Nonthubheko was rushed to after she was burnt. She was admitted to the old burns unit where she was seen to by Dr Henk Kruger.

Dr Kruger on seeing Nothubheko for the first time
V/O: The biggest challenge to treating Nonthubheko (and other paediatric burns victims) was the dilapidated state of the old unit.

Dr Kruger & Dr Madlala on the state of the old burns unit
V/O: Two years ago, the Carte Blanche Making A Difference Trust stepped in to assist. Since its inception in 2008, the trust has raised over R130 million for projects that has significantly reduced infant mortality

When the trust learnt of the challenges facing paediatric burn patients at Ngwelezana, something had to be done as patron of the trust Karolina Andropoulos explains

Karolina on how the Ngwelezana project was started


V/O: Due to its out-dated design, renovating the existing burns ward was not possible. Another plan was needed.

Karolina & Dr Madlala on visiting the old Ophthalmology clinic

V/O: The result was the second largest build in the trust’s history: a dedicated paediatric burns unit built thanks to a capital donation of R10.3 million from South 32’s Hillside Aluminium.

Calvin Mkhabela South 32 spokesmen on how they got involved

V/O: A project of this scale required more than South 32’s principle donation. Additional support from close to 40 material, medical equipment and professional skill-set donors was needed to build the new unit.

Comments from Dr Gil Mahlati (Sakhiwo Health Solutions) & Hendre van Heerden (RCA) on their contribution to the project

V/O: One of the aims of the project was to build a modern state of the art facility as project architect Rudolph Coetzee from Hospital Design Group explains.

Rudolph Coetzee, architect on planning the ward


V/O: Finally, 2 years after the project was first started, the Ngwelezana Paediatric Burns Unit officially opened last month.

After the cutting of the ribbon, stakeholders, partners as well as members of the media were given a tour of the new facility.

Comments from Dr Madlala, Calvin & Gil about how happy they are with the new facility
V/O: It’s been a week since the new paediatric burns unit was officially opened and we’ve returned to see how it runs now that it’s fully operational.

It’s early morning and the day begins with roll-call for the nurses on duty. One of those is Sinenhlanhla Phiri who along with all her colleagues, is thrilled to be working in the new unit.

Intro comment from Sister Phiri about working in the new unit.

V/O: The unit has 22 beds and provides a range of care options, from general patients to high care to isolated ICU rooms.

Sister Phiri & Dr Kruger on the new unit

It also features specialised wet & dry treatment rooms which is crucial to prevent infection

Comment about the importance of the wet & dry room


V/O: Baby Nonthubheko has also enjoyed the benefit of the unit. She and all the children of the old ward were transferred once it became fully operational.

Nokhthula on the care her baby has received in the new unit

Dr Kruger on her prognosis and how the new unit has helped in her recovery.


V/O: After weeks of treatment, she was finally allowed to return home.

V/O: Due to the efforts of Doctors & nurses at Ngwlezana Hospital, little Nothubheko is expected to make a full recovery thanks in no small measure, to the care she received at the new Paediatric Burns Unit.

To be seriously burnt is a truly traumatic event. Now that the Carte Blanche Making A Difference Trust has handed the unit over to the KZN Department of Health, thousands of children have access to one of the best paediatric burns units in the country that the trust hopes will save & improve the lives of countless children now and into the future.
